content:
incidents-bot: Pager: DED-POOL GPU node kernel panic detected in pool aurelia-ded-01 (node ded-node-gpu-7). ~60% of tenant requests are failing with 503s. Severity: P1
samir: Ack. I'm oncall. Paging eng-sre and infra. What's current customer impact? @kevin from CS please stand by
kevin: seeing spikes in errors for Aurelia Labs (tenant id: aurelia-123). They've reported timeouts on production model endpoints. I'm on standby to notify them after triage
rachel: I have node logs. kernel panic at gpu_driver+0x3a1. NVML shows ECC recoverable errors then a panic. Attaching tail of dmesg dump:
```
[ 1324.567890] NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCIe Fault) 79
[ 1324.568001] NVRM: GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1324.568112] kernel panic - not syncing: GPU watchdog
```
infra-bot: Metrics snapshot: node ded-node-gpu-7 memory pressure 94%, temp GPU1=92C, PCIe errors 14 in last 10m. Health: UNHEALTHY
samir: Ok plan: cordon+drain node, evict affected pods, failover tenant traffic to aurelia-ded-01-backup. Who can run the drain command? ops-maya? @deploy-bot can you confirm spare capacity in that pool?
deploy-bot: Spare capacity confirmed: 2 spare nodes available, autoscaler will not trigger during drain. Snapshot of active workloads shows 3 Aurelia replica sets on node.
ops-maya: I'll run the drain now. Command I'm using:
```
rictl node cordon ded-node-gpu-7 --pool=aurelia-ded-01
rictl node drain ded-node-gpu-7 --force --evict-grace=30s
```
ops-maya: starting drain... pods are evicting. Moving Aurelia inference replicas to ded-node-gpu-9 and ded-node-gpu-10
rachel: while draining, set routing policy to route Aurelia model traffic to model-variant low-latency fallback to reduce memory footprint:
```
route set --tenant=aurelia-123 --model=prod-llm:v2 --policy=fallback:model-llm-small
```
samir: good. @kevin prepare brief customer message: incident detected, nodes being drained, failover in progress, no data lost, expect reduced latency for 10-15m, further update in 30min
kevin: drafting now. Message: "We detected a hardware failure in your dedicated pool. Our engineers are draining the affected node and failing over workloads to spare capacity. You may see transient 503s and slight latency changes for ~15 minutes. We'll update with postmortem." Share? :thumbsup:
kevin: sending to AureliaOps@aurelia.com now. They acknowledged.
infra-bot: Drain completed. Node marked DRAINED. Evicted 3 pods. No pod restarts on node. ded-node-gpu-7 health=MAINT
deploy-bot: Failover complete. Routing adjusted. Aurelia endpoint errors dropped to baseline (0.5%) and latency back within SLO. Rolling back fallback in 10m if stable.
samir: Confirm we should reprovision or replace node? Rachel any signs this is transient (driver) vs hardware? If hardware, schedule replace and allocate replacement GPU node.
rachel: PCIe ECC counts and temps suggest thermal-induced hardware failure; driver stack reported GPU reset failed. Recommend replace node before returning to pool. I'll open hardware ticket with provider and flag for replacement.
ops-maya: I've quarantined node from autoscaler and added it to maintenance. Marking for replacement ticket #HW-9832
samir: handing incident to rachel and ops-maya for follow-up and customer postmortem. I'm off at 04:00Z — please escalate back to me if SLA breach projected.
rachel: will run stress test on replaced node before rejoin. Postmortem owners: rachel (root cause & fix), ops-maya (hardware replace), kevin (customer comms). I'll create postmortem doc and link here.
kevin: customer asked for ETA on full service restoration. I told them 2 hours for node replacement and final confirmation after stress test.
samir: thanks team. incident P1 -> mitigated. Switching channel to #postmortems/aurelia-123 for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
incidents-bot: Incident automatically closed in channel incidents; follow-ups tracked in #postmortems/aurelia-123
